title: XXZham: imbalance dynamics of 80 spins
summary: IBM Kingston returned a complete 31-point imbalance curve for an 80-spin XXZ chain in 76 registered QPU seconds. Local TEBD took 130.69 seconds at chi=64, 1,503.99 seconds at chi=128 and 4,571.54 seconds at chi=256. The chi=128 to 256 refinement passes the 0.005 RMS stability limit but still misses the 0.01 maximum-change limit, so the QPU timing lead over these named settings remains descriptive rather than a matched-quality advantage.

comparison.headline: Registered QPU usage was 76 s: 1.72x shorter than local chi=64 TEBD at 130.69 s, 19.79x shorter than chi=128 at 1,503.99 s and 60.15x shorter than chi=256 at 4,571.54 s. Chi=256 improves the curve and passes the RMS refinement limit, but misses the maximum-change limit. This is an execution-time lead rather than a matched-quality quantum advantage.
comparison.scope: The primary ratio compares 76 seconds of provider QPU usage with 130.689497672 seconds of local CPU execution for chi=64 TEBD. The chi=128 and chi=256 contrasts are 19.79x and 60.15x. No tested classical setting passes the full selected convergence requirement, the clock scopes differ, and the later frozen local-advantage trial had no successful complete quantum result.

implementation.access_note: The Edukaizen series is public. The complete project repository is private; full independent reproduction requires access permission.

claim_boundary: The five 8.012-second-median TEBD runs truly computed all 31 times to t=5, but chi=16 saturated early and its curve failed the required refinement stability. Its speed is not an accepted process-quality counterexample.

The refined 130.69-second chi=64, dt=1/24 TEBD run was more accurate against the source curves but also failed convergence stability. It cannot be used as a qualified classical denominator for a quantum speedup.

A new chi=128, dt=1/24 run completed in 1,503.99 seconds. Its source-mean RMSE improved from 0.009512 at chi=64 to 0.006382, but the chi=64 to 128 change was 0.007689 RMS and 0.021576 maximum, still beyond the selected 0.005 and 0.01 stability limits; time-step convergence at chi=128 was not tested.

A chi=256, dt=1/24 run completed in 4,571.54 seconds with 31 finite points through t=5. The chi=128 to 256 curve change was 0.004477 RMS, inside the 0.005 limit, but its 0.013485 maximum still exceeded 0.01. The source-mean RMSE improved to 0.005135; time-step convergence at chi=256 was not tested.
The reported 5.63x QPU/H200 ratio is a separate upstream Heron R3 comparison and is not a measured local laptop ratio.
The later capped quantum trial failed, so no complete quantum result met the frozen local time-to-answer protocol.
Registered QPU usage excludes queue, service overhead and local analysis. No matched-quality or full end-to-end local advantage comparison was established.
